value.title: Plan, up and show, with warnings (workstream 008 s02)
value.summary: `pij pod plan` prints the whole pod and every warning with its fix and writes nothing; `pij pod up` starts each slot through `spawn --as`, canaries each slot's tools, warns and still starts; `pij pod show` reads the pod folder and the database.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: `pij pod plan` prints the whole pod and every warning with its fix and writes nothing; `pij pod up` starts each slot through `spawn --as`, canaries each slot's tools, warns and still starts; `pij pod show` reads the pod folder and the database.

sections.name: goals
value: Plan, confirm, up: a recurring group of seats in one command, with every problem named and nothing silently refused.

value.claim: `pij pod plan <template-path> --set <name>=<value>...` prints each slot's seat with its model and first turn, each consulted role and whether it has a live holder, each deliverable and its owner, and each warning with the command that fixes it: a consulted role needed before up with no live holder (`pij spawn --as role:<id>`), a reviewing slot on its author's model, a deliverable whose owner role is missing (`pij directory add ...`), and the tools each slot will be checked for. It writes nothing and launches nothing.

`pij pod up <template-path> --set ...` creates the pod folder, then starts each slot as `pij spawn --as role:<id>` does (plan 242), once per slot. Each warning is printed with its fix and written to the pod's log; up never refuses on one. It creates no branch or worktree. `--no-start` creates the pod only; `pij spawn --as role:<id> --pod <pod>` starts one member into it.

Tool canary: after a slot's seat starts, pij sends it one message asking it to confirm each tool the slot names, and waits a bounded time on a subscription for the answer. A slot that does not confirm every tool is degraded, shown with the missing tools and the fix in up's report, the log and show; pij hands it no pod work (a brake on pij's own dispatch, not a gate on the prime, whose messages still reach it).
`pij pod show <pod>` lists members with their types, seats and states (from the database), consulted roles, deliverables with owners, and degraded slots with their fixes.
Cost: up launches one spawn per slot and nothing for a consulted role; plan and show launch nothing; the canary is one message and one bounded wait per new seat. No loop, poll or timer.
value.note: live receipt at 387362db (deployed): pij-rs --json ping .data.spawns 546→548 over 20 s idle (+2 ps.registration-native-process, background); one `pod up` of a 1-slot pod 548→579: +4 tmux (new-window, rename-window, pipe-pane attach, set-options tap owner: one spawn) and +27 writer launches (git.community +21, ddocs.community +6: record, role, members commits); then 579→581 over 20 s (+2 background). plan, show, activity, sessions: 581→581. just spawn-rate --seconds 20: no daemon children sampled.

value.title: Plan, up and show, with warnings (workstream 008 s02)

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: spawn --as (crates/daemon/src/http/spawn_role.rs) and the first turn (plan 241); live seats and holders from the store; the memory turn's bounded wait (http/memory_turn.rs) is the model for the canary's wait.

value.risk: A seat never answers the canary.
value.mitigation: The wait is bounded; the slot is degraded with the fix and the pod still runs.
Each is in the pod's log and show, with its fix.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Cost: up: one spawn per slot, one canary message and one bounded wait per new seat; plan, show: no launch. No loop, poll or timer.
No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
